# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue with his heart that requires regular monitoring to ensure stability and control.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences unpredictable bowel movements, but managing his diet helps reduce the issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences more frequent falls compared to others, which is a concern.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear recently, which was treated, and now his ear health is closely monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board during lessons at school and has trouble focusing on distant objects.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with chewing harder foods and has trouble with meat or crunchy fruits and vegetables.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision problems may affect his learning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter than average fingers, which sometimes makes grasping certain objects tricky.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental health and address any concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing health.
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems and provide appropriate treatment.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition and adjust treatment as necessary.
* Consider referral for a skeletal review to assess spinal health and address any concerns.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any behavioural differences.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than other kids her age, suggesting potential cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, with varying interest in food, making mealtimes a daily challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has episodes where she stares off into space, not responding for a few seconds, and these episodes seem to pass on their own.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in her ear, which is being monitored by doctors to see if it clears up on its own or needs further treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when looking at things, and her eyes get strained easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to go to the dentist pretty regularly to prevent any major issues from developing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally behind other children her age, and speech hasn't progressed as expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is developmentally behind other children her age, and speech hasn't progressed as expected.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and prevent dental issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor and address any hearing concerns.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess cardiac function.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess bone age and skeletal structure.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental and behavioural needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an issue with one of her heart valves, which requires close monitoring by a cardiologist to prevent major complications. The parent tries to limit her from exerting herself too much physically.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Some may require surgery, while others only need monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experienced feeding difficulties as a baby, which included pushing food out or not wanting to eat at all. However, this phase passed, and eating has become more manageable over time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences episodes where she stares off into space and doesn't respond for a few seconds, which are frightening for her parents. The cause and how to help her through these moments are still being figured out.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which can be of varying types and typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tendency to turn the volume up really high on the TV or her tablet, indicating potential hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss. Many children have required multiple grommet insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear, and some have still required hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a habit of sitting extremely close to the television or when reading books, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery to bring the eyes into line.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth compared to other kids her age, which may affect her smile and overall dental health long-term. The dentist recommends monitoring them closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel. Regular dental check-ups are important, especially for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety. Medication(s) may be appropriate in some circumstances.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient stands and walks with a slightly odd posture, which has persisted over time and may need to be addressed to prevent future spinal issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine. Many people with KBG syndrome have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers. A small number of children have had hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's large front teeth and overall dental health.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the patient's heart valve issue.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for any spinal or skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity, and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, I'm so worried about his eyesight. He has myopia, and it's been affecting his ability to see things clearly, especially when he's trying to watch TV or play with toys that are far away. I just want to make sure he gets the right help.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes... he seems to hear some sounds but not others clearly. It's like he's filtering out certain noises or frequencies. We've noticed it's harder for him to respond when there's background noise, and that makes me really anxious about his hearing.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: His teeth... they have weak enamel. We have to be super careful with sugary foods and drinks because his teeth can decay easily. I feel guilty sometimes because I know how much he loves sweets.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: The septal defect... it's a constant worry for us. We go for regular check-ups to monitor it, and the doctors say it could potentially lead to more serious issues if not managed properly. Just thinking about it makes me nervous.

Parent: N/A.

Parent: N/A.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect which is a constant worry and requires regular check-ups to monitor it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding aversion, which makes meal times stressful due to certain textures and tastes that he refuses.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which started a few months ago and are not too frequent but are terrifying for the parents.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, seeming to hear some sounds but not others clearly, and has trouble responding to sounds with background noise.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, affecting his ability to see things clearly, especially at a distance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on his teeth, requiring careful brushing and avoidance of sugary foods and drinks to prevent decay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and struggles with clarity when trying to talk.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and an increased curvature of the spine.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage weak enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to address conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to correct myopia and other vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect
* Neurological management to control seizures
* Speech therapy to address speech delay and difficulties
* Behavioral therapy to manage any behavioral differences
* Occupational therapy to help with fine motor skills and feeding aversion
* Physiotherapy to support overall development and mobility

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural abnormality in her heart, which requires regular monitoring by a specialist to prevent it from getting worse.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery and others needing monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, gets upset easily during mealtimes, which affects her appetite and digestion. 
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes stares off into space like she's in a trance, which is worrying because the cause is unknown. She also has coordination issues, moving differently than other kids her age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had an ear infection (otitis media) in the past, which seemed to clear up with antibiotics, and there are ongoing concerns about potential hearing issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems to have trouble seeing things clearly, with a potential diagnosis of astigmatism pending further tests.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, requiring extra care to prevent more dental problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth, necessitating regular dental check-ups, especially with a specialist SEN dentist for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues and moves differently than other kids her age, and experiences feeding difficulties that affect her behavior.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities and coordination issues that affect her movement.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers (brachydactyly), and curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), with a small number having hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in the first few years, to catch and manage any hearing issues early.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct any vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor the heart condition.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to identify any skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed to support development and manage challenges.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structurally abnormal heart, a type of abnormality that requires regular monitoring by a cardiologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences slower growth rate and doesn't gain weight as quickly as his peers, despite eating well.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A very small number of children have required longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences epileptic seizures that started a couple of years ago and are being managed by neurologists.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear last year, which seemed to clear up but may not be fully gone now.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which means he can see really close up but farther away gets blurry.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with chewing, especially with harder foods, and needs to cut everything into small pieces.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which requires careful brushing and regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities and a delayed closure of the soft spot on his head.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental concerns and prevent issues.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart condition.
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to monitor for skeletal abnormalities.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and manage symptoms.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve abnormality in his heart that the cardiologist is keeping an eye on. Regular check-ups are scheduled to monitor its progression.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, and the family is trying different strategies to help manage it, including diet adjustments and establishing a consistent bowel routine.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was developmentally slower to reach certain milestones like walking or sitting compared to his peers. However, with time and support, he's making progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had a glue ear, which has affected his hearing somewhat. The doctors have been monitoring it, and the family is waiting to see how it develops.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has mentioned struggling to see the board at school, particularly during lessons, and often squints or leans forward, possibly indicating a vision issue that needs addressing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has complained about tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods, and the family is planning to take him to a dentist soon.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a speech delay, and regular therapy sessions are helping with his speech development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was developmentally slower to reach certain milestones, but with time and support, he's making progress.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor the glue ear and potential hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor the valve abnormality
* Referral for a skeletal review to assess hip dysplasia and potential spinal issues
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental progress
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Management of constipation through diet adjustments and establishment of a consistent bowel routine

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient occasionally experiences episodes of unusual staring or blank spells, which are concerning and under investigation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had recurring issues with fluid in the ear, which is a common problem in KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with eyesight, often squinting or leaning forward to see better, indicating potential issues such as astigmatism, myopia, or hypermetropia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but potentially transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding difficulties, showing aversion to certain foods or textures, which has limited her diet and caused frustration during meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with her hearing, being able to pick up on some sounds but struggling with others, and it's not consistent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which means she has trouble seeing things that are far away.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges with chewing, especially with harder foods, and tends to avoid those or takes a long time to chew them.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and speech difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address any dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to assess and manage any hearing issues.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to correct any vision problems.
* Consider a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to assess heart condition.
* Speech therapy to address speech difficulties.
* Occupational therapy to help with feeding and dietary challenges.
* Physiotherapy to support developmental delays and motor skills.
* Behavioural therapy to manage any behavioural differences.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulties with feeding and eating, which has been a significant challenge.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays, including slower achievement of milestones such as sitting and walking.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Developmental delay has been reported in almost all children with KBG syndrome, with the degree of delay ranging from mild to severe.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with fluid buildup in the ears.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects the focusing of his eyes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak teeth that break or chip easily.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has developmental delays and slower achievement of milestones.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than expected.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent further weakening.

* Cardiac review to investigate potential heart conditions.
* Consideration of a skeletal review to assess spinal and hip health.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences.
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has seizures that are being managed with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media last year and is being monitored for any further issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV or books, suggesting potential eyesight issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has large front teeth, which may affect his smile and bite.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large permanent upper middle teeth, and may experience weak enamel and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

* Monitoring of the patient's growth velocity and consideration of referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support the patient's development and address any challenges.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient’s speech delay and other developmental issues may impact his educational progress.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a speech delay and was developmentally slower to reach certain milestones.

* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy may be beneficial to address developmental delays and speech issues.
* Regular monitoring for hip dysplasia and potential future intervention.

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular cardiac check-ups with a cardiologist to monitor heart health.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues, managed through diet changes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered spinal cord, which is being monitored by a neurologist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing concerns, with a tendency to turn the TV up loud, indicating potential hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia (nearsightedness), affecting his ability to see things far away.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires regular dental check-ups and treatments due to ongoing teeth issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some experience a variety of other dental concerns, including large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome often require extra help in school, with some attending mainstream primary school and others requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioral differences, and learning difficulties, with some experiencing autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia, which may impact mobility and requires management with an orthopedic specialist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups and treatments
* Regular hearing reviews
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review
* Cardiac review (including echo and ECG)
* Skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull)
* Monitoring for tethered cord
* Management of constipation issues through diet changes
* Orthopedic management for hip dysplasia
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy as needed.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a structural issue with his heart, requiring careful management of overexertion and regular breaks during playtime.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties, is picky about what he eats, and sometimes shows no interest in food, making it hard to ensure he gets enough nutrients.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a lack of interest in feeding being a significant and long-lasting issue for some.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than his peers during physical activities, and has shorter fingers affecting his ability to grasp certain objects or perform finer motor tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, and some have neurological differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is overwhelmed by loud noises, gets frustrated easily in crowded or noisy areas, and has conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a hard time seeing the board in class, even when sitting right up front, indicating potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges with chewing, especially with tougher foods, and avoids them or asks for them to be cut into smaller pieces.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns, requiring regular dental check-ups and careful brushing.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision problems may affect his learning if not addressed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but potentially requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP) for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's hearing and vision difficulties may contribute to frustration and avoidance of certain situations.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has noticeably shorter fingers than average, affecting his ability to grasp certain objects or perform finer motor tasks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, leading to increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and many have short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5, and as needed thereafter, to address conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to assess and correct vision problems.
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor and manage heart conditions.
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess for skeletal anomalies.
* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and address specific challenges.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing and increased heart rate during playtime, suggesting potential cardiac issues that are being monitored by a pediatrician.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had poor feeding as an infant, with challenges in latching and feeding without distress, which improved over time with support.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds, with a very small number needing longer-term tube feeding.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination challenges, appearing less steady on her feet compared to peers, and is undergoing physical therapy and exercise to address this.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments, though in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had fluid in her ear, which caused temporary discomfort and possibly affected her hearing, but the issue resolved after treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss, with many children requiring multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, affecting her ability to see things far away and impacting her focus in class and activities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint, with treatment options including patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger than typical front teeth, with a focus on proper dental care to prevent future issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Besides large front teeth, there can be weak enamel and other dental concerns, emphasizing the importance of regular dental check-ups, especially for those with significant sensory issues.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with most attending mainstream primary school but possibly transferring to special schooling or requiring Educational Health Care Plans for secondary school.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay and behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, with medication sometimes being appropriate.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a delayed closure of her fontanelle, which is being closely monitored to prevent further complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones leading to scoliosis, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers, with a small number experiencing hip dysplasia.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental concerns.
* Regular hearing reviews up to age 5 to catch and treat any hearing issues early.
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to address vision problems.

* Referral for a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, following diagnosis.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis.
* Monitor growth velocity, and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support development and address challenges.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, including not responding immediately to his name and requiring loud noises to get his attention.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often squints when looking at things, especially in bright environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, including astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has been diagnosed with otitis media, an inflammation of the middle ear, which has been causing her some discomfort and occasional fever.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has complained that things appear blurry to her, and an appointment with an optometrist has been scheduled to get her eyes checked.

* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any related concerns.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with a hole in the heart, which requires regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient does not grow like other kids and does not put on weight as expected, despite eating the same food.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences stares or zoning out, which is a concern for the parent.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which can be treated with anti-epileptic medications.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble hearing soft voices and turns up the TV volume to hear everything.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems, including squinting, which suggests potential issues with focus or vision.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are weak and may break easily.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioral differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with hip issues and has a palate anomaly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including short fingers, curved fingers, and hip dysplasia.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth strength and enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor heart condition.
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess skeletal anomalies.
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address behavioral concerns.
